threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'Clapton Park'. Around here, it’s just 'The Park'—everyone knows which one.
Last night on the 196, I saw a guy reciting Shakespeare to a bus stop. Only in Brixton do you get poetry at 3 AM while waiting for a bus.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The way the kebab shop owner remembers my order by heart after just a few visits hit different. That's when I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a random shisha bar that doubles as an art gallery, complete with live performances on a Tuesday night.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local when they refuse to call it 'Delores Park' and instead say 'Mission Park' like it’s always been.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a glimpse of a pigeon purposely hopping over a sleeping man's leg on the bus—only in San Francisco does even the wildlife have swag.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the bohemian vibe, but most locals just want their café con leche without the crowd and noise.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their bewilderment when asked for a ‘cafè amb llet’ instead of just milk. That look is priceless.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus will get you anywhere on time. The locals know to check the app before braving the 38 or the 48.
Caught a glimpse of a man in a tuxedo on the 196, intently reading a novel about hedgehogs. Only in Brixton at 2 AM, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Walking past the old haunted-looking cinema at night, I saw a group of kids huddled over a fire in the alley, laughing like there was no tomorrow.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find a bar made entirely from reclaimed subway tiles, complete with a DJ spinning vinyl from a forgotten era.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can always tell the locals—they roll their eyes when a bus is late, but the transplants are still staring at their apps like there's any hope.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a glimpse of a guy serenading the bus with a ukulele at 7th and Market. Only in SF does the Muni stop feel like a concert.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real vibe is in the hidden plazas where locals sip vermut and chat well into the night.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They stand at the corner of Carrer de Casanova, bewildered, staring at the menú del día like it’s an ancient scroll.
